Manifester sa mauvaise humeur, son mécontentement, maugréer, protester.

examples.text: Il a rouspété quand le patron lui a dit qu’il n’aurait pas d’augmentation cette année.
13 août 1940 – J’adore rouspéter. Ne réussissant jamais à me mettre en colère, ce petit filet de mauvaise humeur me libère
C’est là qu’on se retrouve, les doigts collants : on a huit ans. On rouspète pour la forme, mais un sourire imperceptible monte aux lèvres. On ne se dépêche pas trop d’aller se laver les mains.

glosses: (einer anderen Person) seinen Ärger kundtun

examples.text: Die Zuschauer schimpften laut über den Schiedsrichter.
„Geschimpft wurde und wird immer und überall.“

glosses: mit aggressiven oder beleidigenden Worten tadeln

examples.text: Die Frau schimpft mit ihrem Mann: „Trinke nicht soviel Wein, du alter Säufer!“.

glosses: jemanden, sich oder etwas auf eine bestimmte Weise benennen

examples.text: Seit wenigen Wochen schimpft er sich Meister.
Er schimpft ihn einen ewigen Betrüger.
„Sie wollte fast schon die Zunge hinausstrecken, um von dem Moor zu kosten, verkniff sich den Wunsch dann aber doch. Die Mama sollte sie nicht dumm und neugierig schimpfen.“
Und sowas schimpft sich nun Freundschaft!

translations.source_sense_description: Manifester sa mauvaise humeur, son mécontentement, maugréer, protester.

glosses: sich (oft) gehässig, aber nicht aggressiv beschweren; etwas bekritteln

examples.text: Die Kinder meckern mal wieder über das Essen.

glosses: den typischen Laut einer Ziege (das Meckern) von sich geben

examples.text: Hunde bellen, Katzen miauen, Schafe blöken und Ziegen meckern.

glosses: auf eine alberne Art und Weise lachen oder sprechen

translations.source_sense_description: Manifester sa mauvaise humeur, son mécontentement, maugréer, protester.

glosses: Any pain in the belly, stomach, or abdomen.

examples.text: Eating too much candy can give you a bellyache.

glosses: To unnecessarily complain or whine, often about simple matters.

examples.text: Quit bellyaching about the problem and help us fix it.

translations.source_sense_description: Manifester sa mauvaise humeur, son mécontentement, maugréer, protester.

glosses: A low thundering, rumbling or growling sound.
The sound made by a hungry stomach.
A surly complaint.

examples.text: That whiner is never without a grumble to share.

glosses: To make a low, growling or rumbling noise, like a hungry stomach or certain animals.

examples.text: The distant thunder grumbles.
It made his stomach grumble in protest to think the mule was eating, and here he was worrying about her with an empty belly of his own.

glosses: To complain; to murmur or mutter with discontent; to make ill-natured complaints in a low voice and a surly manner.

examples.text: He grumbles about the food constantly, but has yet to learn to cook.

glosses: To utter in a grumbling fashion.

examples.text: He grumbled that there was no grain "in the country" and that people were talking instead of working to provide it.

translations.source_sense_description: Manifester sa mauvaise humeur, son mécontentement, maugréer, protester.

glosses: An opening through which gases, especially air, can pass.

examples.text: the vent of a cask; the vent of a mould
According to geologists who work in the area, the vents at Castello Aragonese have been spewing carbon dioxide for at least several hundred years, maybe longer.

glosses: A small aperture.

examples.text: Look, how thy wounds do bleed at many vents.
There, at one Paſſage, oft you might ſurvey / A Lye and Truth contending for the vvay; / And long 'tvvas doubtful, both ſo cloſely pent, / VVhich firſt ſhould iſſue thro the narrovv Vent: […]

glosses: An opening in a volcano from which lava or gas flows.
A rant; a long session of expressing verbal frustration.
The excretory opening of lower orders of vertebrates; cloaca.
A slit in the seam of a garment.
The opening at the breech of a firearm, through which fire is communicated to the powder of the charge.
In steam boilers, a sectional area of the passage for gases divided by the length of the same passage in feet.
Opportunity of escape or passage from confinement or privacy; outlet.
Emission; escape; passage to notice or expression; publication; utterance.

examples.text: without the vent of words
Thou didst make tolerable vent of thy travel.

glosses: To allow gases to escape.

examples.text: The stove vents to the outside.

glosses: To allow gases to escape from (a sealed space, container, etc.).

examples.text: In the engine room, the changing angle dropped the melted core to the deck. The hot mass attacked the steel deck first, burning through that, then the titanium of the hull. Five seconds later the engine room was vented to the sea. The Politovskiy's largest compartment filled rapidly with water. This destroyed what little reserve buoyancy the ship had, and the acute down-angle returned. The Alfa began her last dive.

glosses: To allow to escape through a vent.

examples.text: Exhaust is vented to the outside.

glosses: To express a strong emotion.

examples.text: He vents his anger violently.
Can we talk? I need to vent.

He inveighed against the folly of making oneself liable for the debts of others; vented many bitter execrations against the brother; and concluded with wishing something could be done for the unfortunate family.

But the demonstrators remained defiant, pouring into the streets by the thousands and venting their anger over political corruption, the high cost of living and huge public spending for the World Cup and the Olympics.

“They won’t shut the fuck up about it,” Trump privately vented — referring to conservative influencers and media types lashing out over the Epstein memo — according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter.

glosses: To snuff; to breathe or puff out; to snort.

examples.text: Seest, howe brag yond Bullocke beares, So smirke, so smoothe, his pricked eares?[…] See howe he venteth into the wynd.

glosses: To determine the sex of (a chick) by opening up the anal vent or cloaca.

examples.text: We suspect they’ve vented to medbay and are intending to use some kind of surgical tools to ‘upgrade’ the original Among Us with a bunch of cool new features and levels, instead of starting over from scratch with the sequel.
